title: Fibrant targets detect weak equivalences using specified very good cylinders
statement:
Use model categories, cofibrant and fibrant objects, and trivial fibrations from [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with classes $(C,F,W)$, let $A,B$ be cofibrant objects, and let $u:A\to B$ be any morphism. For each $T\in\{A,B\}$ choose a factorization of the codiagonal
$$T\amalg T\xrightarrow{j_T}I_T\xrightarrow{p_T}T$$
with $j_T$ a cofibration and $p_T$ a trivial fibration (a very good cylinder for $T$); write $e_{T,k}=j_T\mathrm{in}_k$ for $k=0,1$, so $p_Te_{T,k}=1_T$. For every fibrant object $Z$, define $h_I(T,Z)$ to be $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(T,Z)$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by pairs $(H e_{T,0},H e_{T,1})$ for morphisms $H:I_T\to Z$. Precomposition with $u$ induces a well-defined function
$$u^*:h_I(B,Z)\longrightarrow h_I(A,Z),\qquad [b]\longmapsto[b u].$$
For every such choice of the two factorizations, $u\in W$ if and only if $u^*$ is bijective for every fibrant $Z$. No simplicial enrichment, properness, or fibrancy of $A$ or $B$ is assumed.

source.place: A. Joyal, The theory of quasi-categories and its applications (CRM Barcelona, 2008), Appendix E, Proposition E.1.10, proof on printed p. 431: the h(u,X) criterion for cofibrant A,B and fibrant X; justified by Propositions E.1.4 and E.1.8. No Stacks tag.
